item.title: 'It’s not red, it’s magenta': How ThinkPad designers gaslit IBM to save the iconic TrackPoint

item.title: Apple’s iPhone and Mac sales keep growing despite RAM shortages
item.description: Apple's iPhone and Mac sales are on the rise even as a global memory shortage squeezes device makers. In its third-quarter earnings report released on Thursday, Apple revealed that iPhone sales jumped 22 percent to $54.25 billion and Mac sales increased 29 percent to $10.35 billion, driving the company's overall revenue to $109.4 billion. item.title: Judge says Trump admin still lacks evidence for Anthropic ‘supply chain risk’ label
item.description: A federal judge said the Trump administration has not presented enough evidence to justify labeling Anthropic a supply chain risk, casting doubt on the government's ban on its AI technology.

item.title: CareCloud begins to notify hundreds of thousands after hackers stole medical records
item.description: The health tech data giant, which handles vast amounts of patients' medical data, said hackers struck one of its protected health data stores.

item.description: Country music icon Willie Nelson has issued a strongly worded statement about the encroachment of data centers in rural locations across the US.

item.description: Why is Firefox sponsoring Wrexham AFC? The connection between the scrappy football club and struggling web browser is more obvious than you might think. We got to the bottom of it.

item.description: Friend, the AI wearable, can now talk to its users — for an enhanced price.

item.title: One of Wall Street’s most-watched AI investors just sold off all his stocks. Here’s why
item.description: Situational Awareness, a hedge fund run by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, reportedly sold its investments after massive losses. Situational Awareness—an AI-focused hedge fund run by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner—made headlines on Thursday when it sold off investments and was unwinding trades after suffering massive losses on AI and software stocks, according to CNBC, who spoke with people familiar with the situation....

item.title: That cringey LinkedIn post? You can now report it as ‘AI slop’
item.description: The professional networking site is giving users a new way to hide and report posts they believe rely too heavily on artificial intelligence. LinkedIn is pushing back against lengthy, low-quality posts generated with artificial intelligence, also known as “AI slop,” that users have become accustomed to seeing in their feeds.

item.title: A Y-Combinator startup offered job interviews in exchange for getting a tattoo—because they want employees ‘just as crazy as we are’
item.description: AI company LemonLime’s hiring stunt has gone viral for all the wrong reasons, prompting accusations of exploitation. The job market may feel more crowded than ever, but how far would candidates go to set themselves apart? One startup put that to the test, challenging hopeful candidates to get a permanent tattoo in exchange for a guaranteed interview....
